\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage{amsmath}

\begin{document}

\begingroup
The energy of a particle is given by
\[ E = mc^2 \]
where c is the speed of light in vacuum.
\endgroup

\clearpage

\begingroup
The kinematic equations describe uniform acceleration.
\[ v = u + at \]
The second follows from integrating the first.
\[ s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \]
Both assume the acceleration a is constant.
\endgroup

\end{document}

Consider the system $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ with
\[
A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix $A$ is symmetric and positive definite.
\endgroup
